## Push-to-talk is wired — commit `62035052`

**What it does:** hold the bound button anywhere on the site (default: the mouse's thumb/forward button) and a small mic shows up bottom-right, growing with your voice level. Release and it fades out a moment later. Click it any time to jump straight to the dev shell's chat tab. It talks to the same one global dictation session every other surface already shares — no second recording path.

**Built** (`ux/Dictate/push-to-talk.js` + `FloatingMic.css`, new):
1. Registers `"dictate.push"` with [Hotkeys](/framework/ux/Hotkeys/) (the sibling minion's module — mouse button 4 default, rebindable).
2. Drives the existing global `chat()` mount's `start_mic()`/`stop_mic()`, with the live level read off `Dictate`'s own already-smoothed `on_meter` number (same one `Widget.Pulse`'s dot uses).
3. The floating mic itself — single gray/primary icon, scales 1.5em→2em by CSS `transform`, never touches layout. (Picked over the owner's two-colour "another idea" as the smaller MVP — noted as a named follow-up, not lost.)
4. A `section("hotkeys", …)` row landed in the drawer's Settings tab.
5. One line in `public/app.js`'s `render()` mounts it everywhere; `navigated()` reports the current page to the session as context.

Also added `devshell.open_tab(name)` (one line, `dev/DevShell/DevShell.js`) so the mic's click can open the shell straight to its chat tab.

**Checked:** every touched/new file passes `node --check`; `http://push-to-talk.localhost/` loads clean (200, screenshot looks normal, mic correctly invisible at rest).

**Left open:** headless proof of the click→down→up gesture itself — that's the next task (`ptt-proof`) per the parent brief.

## Done: `ux/Hotkeys` — a tiny, site-wide hotkey manager

Built, committed, and landed. Live page: `/framework/ux/Hotkeys/`

**What it does:**
- One flat list of named hotkeys — no nested per-panel scopes, matching the owner's own words
- A binding is a keyboard key *or* a mouse button (the owner's thumb button is first-class, not a special case) — back/forward navigation is prevented so the page never jumps away
- Settings UI (`hotkeys_section()`): filter box + one row per action + a "press a key or button…" rebind button
- Saved per browser via `ext/Saver/LocalStorageSaver` (reused, not hand-rolled)

**A real bug caught before landing:** the sibling minion's work (`ux/Dictate/push-to-talk.js`, `ext/drawer/tabs/settings.js`) was already present in this shared worktree. It calls `section("hotkeys", () => hotkeys_section())`, but my first draft had `hotkeys_section()` wrap itself in a second, duplicate title. Found by reading what was already consuming it, fixed before commit — full note in [`doc/decisions.md`](/framework/ux/Hotkeys/doc/decisions/).

**Proof:** page loads 200, zero console errors, zero overflow at 1280/1920/2560/3440 (`Server/layout-check.mjs`). Two commits: `3c5c5958` (the module), `13a14694` (landing the task log).

Left for the next minion, as the brief specified: nothing — that wiring is already in place and checked compatible.

## Open-mic toggle added — commit `28e3f514`

**What's new:** `Ctrl+Shift+M` now toggles an open mic on/off, alongside the existing hold-to-talk (mouse button 4). Press once to start, press again to stop — same floating mic, same global chat session, no second code path.

**Overlap rule:** if you hold push-to-talk while the toggle is already on, releasing it is a no-op — the toggle keeps the mic live. A stray thumb-button tap should never cut off an open-mic session you turned on deliberately.

**On the Hotkeys dependency:** while I was writing this, `hotkeys-module`'s own `Hotkeys.js` was mid-edit in this same shared worktree, adding exactly the modifier-combo shape (`ctrlKey`/`shiftKey`/`altKey`/`metaKey`) the mastermind described — I confirmed the diff matched before committing, and registered against it without touching `ux/Hotkeys/` myself (still their fence).

Only `push-to-talk.js` is staged/committed (+46/-10); page loads clean, `node --check` clean.

## Done: modifier-key follow-up landed

Extended `ux/Hotkeys`' key binding to carry `ctrlKey`/`shiftKey`/`altKey`/`metaKey`, so "Ctrl+Shift+M" is expressible. Commit `7483ff78`.

- **Semantics (documented in [`doc/decisions.md`](/framework/ux/Hotkeys/doc/decisions/)):** an omitted modifier means it must be **up**, not "don't care" — otherwise a bare `M` binding would also fire on every `Ctrl+Shift+M` press.
- `capture()` now records the real modifier state off the captured keydown; `matches()`/`fire()` compare every modifier; `Hotkeys.text()` reads `"Ctrl+Shift+M"`.
- Added a second demo row to the live page so it's shown, not just described.
- Checked `ux/Dictate/push-to-talk.js`'s already-landed `"dictate.toggle"` registration — it uses exactly this shape (`{ type: "key", code: "KeyM", ctrlKey: true, shiftKey: true }`), so no changes needed there.

Proof: 200, `layout-check.mjs` clean at all 4 widths, screenshot shows the real "Ctrl+Shift+M" row. `task.jsonl` and the day log updated; status posted to the owner's live log.

## Summary

**Push-to-talk proof is done, with one real bug found and one architectural risk confirmed.**

- **Root cause (new finding):** the floating push-to-talk mic never appears on a real page load — `push-to-talk.js` builds it before anything has told the page where to put new elements, unlike the two sibling modules (`devbar.js`, `devshell.js`) that defer and attach explicitly. One-line fix named in `proof.md`.
- **Checks 1/2/4** (hold-to-talk, toggle+overlap, click-to-chat): FAIL — blocked entirely by that one bug.
- **Check 3** (level → mic scale): PASS, simulated.
- **Check 5** (settings row + rebind): PASS.
- **Check 6** (no console errors): FAIL on an unrelated, pre-existing 404 — not a push-to-talk regression.
- **Check 7** (cross-mount double-send, added mid-task by @task-mastermind-one-dictation's coordination note): confirmed by reading `chat.js` — two live mounts each send their own `Session.say()` with no cross-mount dedup. This is a `chat.js` design-level risk, not push-to-talk-specific. Live request-count confirmation is still owed — the worktree's own dev server started 502ing mid-task (Servex restarted, unrelated to this work) and hadn't recovered after three retries, and restarting it isn't a minion's call.
